ev.q: with the median prevalence for all states, DC, and Puerto Rico increasing from 4.5% to 8.2%
Based on self-reported data collected during 1995–2010 by the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System
the prevalence of diagnosed diabetes was calculated as the percentage of the population answering "yes"
with the median prevalence for all states, DC, and Puerto Rico increasing from 4.5% to 8.2%
In 2010, median age-adjusted prevalence was highest among states in the South (9.8%) versus states in the Midwest (7.5%)
Estimates were age-adjusted using the 2000 U.S. standard population
ongoing, random-digit–dialed telephone surveys of noninstitutionalized U.S. civilian adults
Trends from 1995–2010 were assessed using BRFSS data.

methods_quotes.q: State-specific and regional trends in age-adjusted diagnosed diabetes prevalence incorporating all 16 years of BRFSS data were assessed using least squares regression.
Linear and quadratic terms for time (year of survey) were included in the models.
Sampling weights and statistical software that account for the complex sampling design of BRFSS were used to estimate state prevalence
Age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population; weighted estimates.
Nonsignificant quadratic terms were dropped from the models.
